summary: A single-user home library app: add books (title, author, category), list all books, lend a book to a named borrower, mark it returned, edit or delete a book, filter to just the lent-out books, and see the current lent-out count. Data persists in localStorage.
implemented_features: Add a book with title, author, and category (novel/cookbook/reference/other)
List all books sorted by title
Lend a book out (record borrower name + date)
Mark a lent book as returned
Filter the collection to just the books currently lent out
Display the count of books currently lent out
Persist all data across refresh via localStorage with malformed-data recovery
assumptions: Single-user, local-computer use: persistence uses browser localStorage rather than any backend, matching the idea's scope.
'Roughly what kind of book' is represented by a fixed set of categories (Novel, Cookbook, Reference, Other) selectable from a list, keeping input simple and consistent.
Lending records only a borrower name and the date the book went out; no due dates or history since the idea only asks to clear it when returned.
The lent-out count is a derived value shown in the header and on the 'Out' filter button, as the idea requests 'how many are lent out right now'.

tests_run.journey: Add a book and see it in the list with the lent-out count at 0
Reject adding a book with empty fields and show validation errors
Lend a book out to a named borrower, filter to lent-out books, then mark it returned
Edit an existing book's title and category
Delete a book that was added by mistake
Preserve books across a component re-mount (localStorage persistence)
Show an empty 'Out' state when filtering with nothing lent out
Prevent lending out with an empty borrower name and show an error
Domain logic: create, validate, lend, return, update, normalize, and count books correctly
Repository: round-trip books through localStorage and drop malformed stored data
